rationale: Review of iteration 3 (reuse of the base chunking pipeline) on diff e2989abb0..d21869acc. All three lenses ran and spec §1 is otherwise satisfied, backed by live and end-to-end evidence. CR-001 is a guardrail-coverage regression introduced by moving the header into metadata. CR-002 covers two test gaps that the acceptance lens marked as partial. Deferred (4): the header is not token-capped (already listed in the MR trade-offs); the on_split_documents monitoring estimate excludes the repeated header; there is no defensive fallback for an empty body (unreachable for assistants, whose body always contains 'Description:'); per-entity chunk-count logging. Dismissed (9): shared-dict mutation (the base copies metadata per chunk); 'abstract interface changed' (it was reverted to main's); orphans from 0-based ids (the stale cleanup removes them, as shown live); numbering-reset concurrency (a processor is created per call); the return-count semantics (same as main); disallowed_special={} (the base convention); the hardcoded o200k_base (the base convention); the processor-to-loader-constant import (no cycle, tests import fine); section labels only in the first chunk (inherent to splitting).

findings.title: Header text bypasses knowledge-base guardrails
findings.problem: _process applies _apply_guardrails_for_documents to the whole documents. Guardrails mask or block document.page_content only. After the refactor, page_content is the body alone; the header (name, slug, project, categories, toolkits, 'Created by: <username>', usage) lives in metadata and is prepended later in _process_chunk.
findings.impact: Header text, including the creator username, is embedded and stored in ES without passing configured guardrails such as PII masking or blocking. This is a regression from main and from iteration 2, where the header was part of page_content.
findings.recommendation: Apply guardrails to the final chunks: call _apply_guardrails_for_documents(chunks) after _split_entity_documents in _process, so the embedded text is exactly the guarded text. Add a test proving that header text is passed to guardrails.

findings.title: Spec test gaps: last tool after split; 0-based storage fixtures
findings.problem: TestSplitEntityDocuments does not assert that the last tool name survives splitting, and the _doc/_chunks fixtures number chunks from 0, so the expected ids look like a_0.
findings.impact: The spec Testing section is not fully met, and the fixtures show a chunk-id convention the code no longer produces.
findings.recommendation: Add a long tools list to the long-entity split test and assert that the last tool is present. Make _chunks 1-based and update the expected ids to _1..N.
